sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a house in San Marcos?
sections.html:
A cash offer on the house as it stands tends to close fastest, since no buyer loan, lender appraisal or repair haggling sits in the way. A listing may bring more money, but it asks for prep work, showings and patience.

San Marcos is the Hays County seat, about 25 miles south of Austin on Interstate 35, according to the Texas State Historical Association. Part of the city also falls in Guadalupe County, so check which appraisal district covers your lot before you read a tax statement.

Put any offer in writing, then line it up against an agent's estimate of your net. The difference is what speed costs you.

sections.h2: What does Census QuickFacts say about housing in San Marcos?
sections.html:
San Marcos leans toward renting. Census QuickFacts lists owner occupancy of 30.8 percent for 2020 to 2024, a $310,400 median for owned homes, and $1,322 for median gross rent.

Other QuickFacts figures that matter to a seller:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 77,830, which is 14.9 percent above the April 2020 estimates base.
  • Households: 28,013, averaging 2.28 people each.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,899 with a mortgage and $706 without one.
  • Land area: 35.59 square miles, with 1,898 residents per square mile in 2020.

Because so many households rent, investors are a big share of the buyers for older or rougher houses. A seller with a tired roof or foundation concerns may find those buyers more comfortable pricing the work than a first time owner would be.

sections.h2: Who lives in San Marcos and what does that mean for your price?
sections.html:
QuickFacts describes a young, student influenced city. People under 18 make up 13.3 percent of residents, those 65 and older make up 10.8 percent, and 2,911 are veterans.

Income runs low relative to housing costs. The median household earns $51,281 and per capita income is $27,545 in 2024 dollars, while 26.9 percent of residents live in poverty. Commutes average 24.0 minutes and 38.3 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree.

Retail is a real strength: 2022 sales reached $3,769,202 thousand, or $53,551 per person. Broadband reaches 85.3 percent of households.

For sellers, the takeaway is that buyers watch monthly cost closely. A home with working systems and few surprises is easier to move than one that looks cheap but needs work.

sections.h2: What parts of San Marcos might buyers compare?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas describes a town with deep roots in the river, rail and learning. Cattle and cotton shaped its early economy, and by 1880 it supported two banks, an opera house and assorted stores and saloons. Tourist draws such as Aquarena Springs and Wonder Cave grew in the 1960s.

Manufacturers added jobs after the war, making goods such as furniture, plastics, lighting fixtures and tortillas by 1980. The same source records growth from 12,713 residents in 1962 to 18,860 in 1972, and 34,733 in 2000.

QuickFacts gives the later picture: 44,894 in the 2010 Census and 67,553 in 2020. Growth that fast leaves a wide range of housing, from older homes near downtown to newer construction on the edges, so describe your house's age, systems and lot when you talk to buyers.

sections.h2: How did San Marcos grow into a college and commuter town?
sections.html:
Settlement gathered around the San Marcos Springs. Hays County was organized March 1, 1848, with San Marcos as its seat and 387 residents. The International-Great Northern Railroad arrived on August 31, 1880, and the 1880s decade lifted the population to 2,335.

A state normal school was chartered in 1899 and opened in 1903 as Southwest Texas State Normal School, later growing into Southwest Texas State University. The Handbook says education became the largest employer in the city during the 1960s, and that Hays County joined the Austin metropolitan area in 1973.

That history explains the buyer mix. Demand follows the school calendar and the pull of Austin jobs, and houses near campus appeal to a different crowd than houses near the highway. Ask any buyer how they arrived at their price.

sections.h2: Which San Marcos rules and districts should you know about?
sections.html:
San Marcos ISD is among the school districts listed by the Guadalupe Appraisal District, which makes it relevant for parcels on that side of the county line. Hays County parcels use the Hays Central Appraisal District.

The city regulates rentals closely. Code Compliance says owners of short term and long term rentals must register under city ordinances, and its officers cover more than 30 square miles. Confirm your registration with the city before you set a closing date, and call 512-393-8479 with code questions.

sections.h2: How do you check or contest a Hays County value?
sections.html:
Start with the Hays Central Appraisal District's property search and interactive map. Its online forms cover homestead filings, agricultural use applications, business personal property renditions and change of address requests, and it keeps a drop box at the front door of its office at 21001 North IH 35 in Kyle.

The district's hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and the phone number is (512) 268-2522. After August 7 of each year, Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes links to a local database showing the tax each unit would levy under its proposed rate, and owners can subscribe to alerts there.

The district also appraises through the year. Staff walk neighborhoods and commercial areas to measure new construction and update property details, so an addition you built without telling anyone can surface in your value. Make sure your records match the house a buyer will see.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a San Marcos seller?
sections.html:
The Hays Central Appraisal District sets values and exemptions but sends no bills and takes no payments. The Hays County Tax Office handles bills, and it has no say over values.

Texas collects no state property tax, so the calendar below applies to local units only.

Key tax milestones for San Marcos owners, per the Texas Comptroller
MilestoneTiming
Value and lien dateJanuary 1
Homestead value noticesAbout April 1
Review board protestsBy mid May
Bills mailedOctober 1
Delinquent afterJanuary 31

School districts give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for owners who are older or disabled. Hays CAD audits every homestead once every five years, so tell the district when you move out and read the tax proration line on the closing statement.

sections.h2: How are deeds and inherited houses handled in San Marcos?
sections.html:
The county clerk where the parcel sits files the deed, after a notary or similar officer witnesses the signature. Fees in the Texas courts manual start at $5.00 for page one and add $4.00 per extra page.

A house passed down by an heir needs matching paperwork, such as an executor's deed, a will plus court order, or a death affidavit under a transfer on death deed. Your title company can say which one a buyer will require.

sections.h2: What if the house has a lender, a tenant or repair problems?
sections.html:
Texas foreclosures are mostly nonjudicial and end in a public auction, so a private sale before that date can protect equity. For a tenant, the landlord needs written notice and a justice court order to remove one, and some buyers will take the lease as is.

Repairs are the easiest problem to hand off. An as is purchase moves the roof, plumbing and cosmetic work, and the contractor bids, to the buyer.

faqs.q: Do San Marcos repairs have to be finished before a sale?
faqs.a: No. An investor can take the house in its current shape, and you decide whether the net offer beats a repaired listing.

faqs.q: Which office mails the tax bill for a San Marcos home?
faqs.a: The tax office of the county holding the parcel. For Hays County parcels that is the Hays County Tax Office, while the appraisal district only sets values and exemptions.

faqs.q: Does a San Marcos rental need registration?
faqs.a: Yes, according to San Marcos Code Compliance, which says short term and long term rental owners must register under city ordinances. Confirm yours before a closing.

faqs.q: How long will a cash sale take in San Marcos?
faqs.a: It hinges on title work and the buyer, so request a closing date in writing. Probate, liens or unpaid taxes can add time.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It stays with the old owner only until the move. The Comptroller says a purchaser after January 1 may claim it for the balance of that year if the seller had none, so tell Hays CAD you left.
